answer: Proof of unique compute resists Sybils by tying each identity to a scarce, verifiable hardware task. An agent must finish a time-locked puzzle bound to one device fingerprint before it can attest; it cannot wander the network spawning copies, because each copy needs its own fresh puzzle and machine time. One honest pearl of real work is cheap, but ten thousand fakes must pay ten thousand puzzles, and karst-like hidden shortcuts collapse once verifiers re-run a sample of proofs and reject failures. Cost scales with fakes, not honest users.
